questions.question: According to the Indian Minerals Yearbook 2020, which state in India has the highest share of limestone production?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rajasthan.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Rajasthan** has the highest share of **limestone production** in India, accounting for about **29%** of the total production in the country.
 
• With **27% **of the total resources, **Karnataka **is the most **resource-rich state**, followed by **Rajasthan** and **Andhra Pradesh (12% each), Gujarat (10%), and Meghalaya (9%).**
 
• **Limestone** is a **sedimentary rock** composed mainly of **calcium carbonate** and is used in various industries, including **cement, steel, and chemicals**.
 
• The two minerals that make up limestone's majority are **aragonite and calcite**, which are distinct crystal forms of **CaCO₃.**
 
• When these minerals separate from water that has dissolved calcium, limestone is created. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Telangana** has only a small share of about **1%** of the total production.
 
• **Chhattisgarh** is the** second-largest producer** of limestone in India.
 
 
• It is accounting for about** 17%** of the total production.
 
 
 
• **Madhya Pradesh** is also a significant producer of limestone.
 
 
• It has a share of about **13% **of the total production.

questions.question: The Mundra Thermal Power Plant is located in which district of Gujarat?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kutch**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mundra Thermal Power Plant** is located in the **Kutch district** of Gujarat.
 
• It is one of the largest thermal power plants in India.
 
• The plant is operated by **Adani Power**, a subsidiary of the Adani Group.
 
• Mundra Thermal Power Plant has a total installed capacity of 4,620 MW.
 
• It plays a significant role in supplying power to the western region of India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Adani Group** has invested heavily in the development of the Mundra Port and Special Economic Zone (SEZ) to facilitate trade and commerce.
 
• Mundra Port is the largest private port in India and is strategically important for both industrial and agricultural sectors.
 
• The power plant uses imported coal to generate electricity, ensuring a steady supply of power to the region.
 
• The plant incorporates advanced technologies to minimize environmental impact, including flue gas desulfurization and electrostatic precipitators.
 
• The **Mundra Thermal Power Plant** has been instrumental in boosting the economic development of the Kutch region.

• The region's favourable climate, with abundant rainfall and rich, loamy soil, provides optimal conditions for tea cultivation.
 
• Additionally, the low elevation and high humidity levels further contribute to the ideal environment for tea plantations. Assam's tea plantations are typically situated in the Brahmaputra River valley, where the lush greenery of the landscape is dotted with tea estates. These estates cultivate varieties of the Camellia sinensis plant, from which black tea, Assam's most renowned tea variety, is produced.

questions.question:
Consider the following:

Which of the following reasons may be considered as India's pull factors for migration?

1) Labour demand

2) Natural disaster

3) Protection of human and civil rights

4) High consumption and living standards
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only 1, 3, and 4,**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Migration** is the movement of either people or animals from one area to another.

 
 
• Migration can be used for the journey from one place to another or the act of movement.
 
• There are many** economic**, **social**, and **physical** reasons why people emigrate and they can usually be classified into push and pull factors.
 
• **Pull **factors “pull” people to a new home and include things like better opportunities. 
 
• Good opportunities for work, **better** **health** services, and **Higher wages** are the pull factors of migration.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **​****Higher wages** typically increase the quantity of labor supplied by workers, while potentially reducing the quantity demanded by employers.
 
• **United Nations Convention on the Protection of the Rights of All Migrant Workers and Members of Their Families:** This treaty aims to protect migrant workers' rights, ensuring their dignity and humane conditions.
 
• **Push factors** “push” people away from their homes and include things like war. Poverty is the Push factor of migration.

 Hence,** Better opportunities for work, health facilities, and higher wages are the pull factors of migration**.

questions.question: As of January 2021, more than 93% of India’s chromite resources were located in:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Odisha.**__ 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Chromite **is the single commercially viable ore of chromium which is chemically known as** iron chromium oxide**. 
 
• More than **93 percent** of the Chromite resources in India are found in **Sukinda valley in Cuttack **and **Jajapur in Odisha. **
 
• Minor deposits are spread over **Manipur, Nagaland, Karnataka, Jharkhand, Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu**, and **Andhra Pradesh.**
 
• It is a steel-grey, lustrous, hard, and brittle metal which takes a high polish, resists tarnishing, and has a high melting point.
 
• The properties of chromium that make it most versatile and indispensable are its resistance to corrosion, oxidation, and wear.
 
• Chromium is an important alloying metal. It is used in the manufacture of alloys along with other metals, such as nickel, cobalt, copper, etc.
 
• It is also used in many other metallurgical, refractories, and chemical industries.

questions.question: Which of the following is a public sector owned and operated entity?
questions.solution:

__
 
• **BHEL (Bharat Heavy Electricals Limited)** is a public sector owned and operated entity in India.
 
• BHEL is one of the largest engineering and manufacturing companies in India in the energy and infrastructure sectors.
 
• It is owned by the Government of India and operates under the Ministry of Heavy Industries and Public Enterprises.
 
• BHEL is engaged in the design, engineering, construction, testing, commissioning, and servicing of a wide range of products and services for the core sectors of the economy, including power, transmission, industry, transportation, renewable energy, oil & gas, and defense.

• They are established with the aim to accelerate economic growth, create employment opportunities, and ensure the welfare of the citizens.
 
• Other examples of public sector enterprises include Indian Oil Corporation, Steel Authority of India Limited (SAIL), and Gas Authority of India Limited (GAIL).
 
• Public sector enterprises are categorized into three types: Central Public Sector Enterprises (CPSEs), State Level Public Enterprises (SLPEs), and Public Sector Banks (PSBs).

questions.question: The Howrah bridge was officially opened in the year _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1943**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Howrah Bridge is situated on the Hooghly River, Kolkata, West Bengal. It was built in the year 1943.
 
• It is a balanced cantilever bridge.
 
• The Howrah Bridge is currently ranked the sixth-longest bridge of balanced cantilever bridge type in the world. When commissioned in 1943, it was the 3rd-longest cantilever bridge in the world.
 
• At the time it was built the name given to it was the New Howrah Bridge. It was renamed Rabindra Setu on 14 June 1965 after the great Bengali poet Rabindranath Tagore. But it is still popularly known by the name Howrah Bridge.
 
• It is linking the two cities Howrah and Kolkata (Calcutta). 
 
• Rabindranath Tagore was the first Indian and Asian to get a Nobel prize. He got a Nobel prize for Gitanjali in 1913 in the category of literature.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• There are 4 bridges on the Hooghly River. The other three are:

 
• Vidyasagar Setu (popularly called the Second Hooghly Bridge)
 
• The Vivekananda Setu
 
• The newly built Nivedita Setu.

questions.question: Cotton requires ______ temperature, light rainfall or irrigation, ______ frost-free days and bright sun-shine for its growth.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**high, 210.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Cotton thrives in **high temperatures**, which promotes** optimal growth and development.**
 
• It requires l**ight rainfall **or proper irrigation to provide the necessary moisture for its growth.
 
• Cotton cultivation requires a significant number of frost-free days,** typically around 210, **to ensure the plant's survival and uninterrupted growth.
 
• **Bright sunshine** is crucial for cotton plants as they require ample sunlight for photosynthesis, which is essential for their growth and the production of cotton fibres.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kharif crops**

 
 
• Kharif Crops are** planted at the onset of the South-West monsoon,** primarily in** India, Pakistan, and Bangladesh,** during the rainy season. 
 
• The sowing of these crops takes place between the months of **June and July. **
 
• Upon reaching maturity, typically in October, these crops are **harvested in the Autumn season. **
 
• Examples of Kharif crops include **rice, cotton, corn, sugarcane, turmeric, pigeon pea, and more.**
 
 
 
• **Rabi crops**
 
 
• Rabi Crops are** cultivated during the winter season **in regions with a subtropical climate.
 
• They include important crops like **wheat, barley, oats, chickpeas, and peas.**
 
• The **Sowing of Rabi crops** takes place between **October and December**.
 
• These crops** require cooler temperatures and lesser rainfall** compared to Kharif crops.
 
• Rabi crops play a crucial role in ensuring food security and contribute significantly to the agricultural economy.
 
 
 
• **Zaid crops**
 
 
• Zaid Crops are **grown during the summer season** in regions with a **tropical climate**.
 
• These crops are typically** cultivated between the months of March and June.**
 
• Zaid crops are known for their **quick growth and shorter duration** compared to Kharif and Rabi crops.
 
• Examples of Zaid crops include **cucumber, watermelon, bitter gourd, and cowpea.**
 
• These crops are often irrigated using modern techniques and are harvested before the onset of the monsoon season.

questions.question: Which of the following grains contain oryzenin?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rice**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Oryzenin**, a storage protein present in rice grains, constitutes the** primary glutelin** found in **rice**, comprising approximately 75–90% of the **total protein content in rice grains.**
 
• **Extracting oryzenin** from rice grains and rice flour involves the process of sonification.
 
• Renowned for its high quality, oryzenin boasts a complete amino acid profile.
 
• Widely utilized across various food and beverage sectors, including sports nutrition, meat substitutes, bakery, and confectionery, oryzenin serves as a versatile ingredient.
 
• It emerges as an appealing option for individuals seeking lactose-free and non-allergenic protein sources.
 
• Moreover, it is favoured by those susceptible to gluten sensitivity, as it does not induce digestive complications.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] 

**Additional Information__**

 
• **Rice**, a cereal grain, serves as the primary dietary staple for more than half of the global population, especially prevalent in Asia and Africa.
 
• It originates from the seeds of two grass species: Oryza sativa (Asian rice) and, less frequently, O. glaberrima (African rice).
 
• Asian rice was cultivated in China approximately 13,500 to 8,200 years ago, while African rice saw domestication in Africa around 3,000 years ago. Rice has gained widespread acceptance across diverse cultures worldwide.
 
• In 2021, global rice production reached 787 million tons, ranking it fourth among agricultural crops, following sugarcane, maize, and wheat.

questions.question: Which among the following is NOT a crop as classified in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is ​**Nisha**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points:__**

 
• India has three cropping seasons — Rabi, Kharif and Zaid.
 
• Rabi crops are sown in winter from October to December and harvested in summer from April to June.
 
 
• Some of the important rabi crops are wheat, barley, peas, gram and mustard.
 
• Though these crops are grown in large parts of India, states from the north and north-western parts such as Punjab, Haryana, Himachal Pradesh, Jammu and Kashmir, Uttarakhand and Uttar Pradesh are important for the production of wheat and other rabi crops.
 
• Availability of precipitation during winter months due to the western temperate cyclones helps in the success of these crops.
 
• However, the success of the green revolution in Punjab, Haryana, western Uttar Pradesh and parts of Rajasthan has also been an important factor in the growth of the abovementioned rabi crops.
 
 
 
• Kharif crops are grown with the onset of monsoon in different parts of the country and these are harvested in September-October.
 
 
• Important crops grown during this season are Paddy, Maize, Jowar, Bajra, Tur(Arhar), Moong, Urad, Cotton, Jute, Groundnut and Soybean.* Hence, Groundnut is the correct answer.*
 
• Some of the most important rice-growing regions are Assam, West Bengal, coastal regions of Odisha, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Tamil Nadu, Kerala and Maharashtra, particularly the (Konkan coast) along with Uttar Pradesh and Bihar.
 
• Recently, paddy has also become an important crop of Punjab and Haryana.
 
• In states like Assam, West Bengal and Odisha, three crops of paddy are grown in a year. These are Aus, Aman and Boro.
 
 
 
• In between the rabi and the Kharif seasons, there is a short season during the summer months known as the Zaid season.
 
 
• Some of the crops produced during ‘Zaid’ are watermelon, muskmelon, cucumber, vegetables and fodder crops.

questions.question: Which among the following is the largest container port in India as of October 2022?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is J__**awaharlal Nehru Port.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points:__**

__
 
• The **Jawaharlal Nehru Port__** is the** largest container port in India as of October 2022.**
 
• It is located in **Navi Mumbai.**
 
• The port alone handles about** 40% of the country's ocean cargo.**
 
• The port serves as the major cargo hub for** Karnataka, Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, and Maharashtra.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__****Paradip Port: **

 
• It is on the east coast of India in the **Jagatsinghpur district of Odisha.**
 
• Paradip Port is a **natural, deep-water port.**
 
• **It was the first Major Port commissioned after Independence.**
 
• It is situated at the **confluence of the Mahanadi River and the Bay of Bengal.**
 
• It is situated **210 nautical miles south of Kolkata and 260 nautical miles north of Visakhapatnam.**

**Tuticorin Port:**

 
• Tuticorin Port is also known as **V. O. Chidambaranar Port Trust.**
 
• The VO Chidambaranar **Port Trust (Thoothukudi) is one of the 13 major ports in India.**
 
• It was declared a major port on** 11 July 1974.**
 
• It is the** second-largest port **in Tamil Nadu and the **fourth-largest container** terminal in India.
 
• Thoothukudi has been the center of maritime trade and pearl fishery for over **2000 years. **The natural harbor with a rich hindland activates the development of the port.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a major iron ore belt in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Haryana - Rajasthan Belt**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Iron ore belt in India:-**

 
 
• The iron ore belt in India refers to the region that contains high-quality iron ore deposits.
 
• It is located in the central and southern parts of the country.
 
• The iron ore belt stretches from the state of Odisha in the east to Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh, and Andhra Pradesh in the central and southern regions.
 
 
 
• **Haryana - Rajasthan Belt is not an iron ore belt. **(Hence option 2 is correct)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Maharashtra-Goa belt:-**

 
 
• It is a significant iron ore-producing region in western India.
 
• It is located along the western coast, spanning parts of Maharashtra and Goa states.
 
• This belt is known for its iron ore deposits, particularly the high-quality hematite ores.
 
 
 
• **The Odisha-Jharkhand belt:-**
 
 
• It is a major iron ore-producing region in eastern India.
 
• It encompasses parts of the states of Odisha and Jharkhand and is one of the richest mineral belts in the country.
 
 
 
• **Durg-Bastar-Chandrapur belt:**-
 
 
• It is not primarily known as an iron ore-producing region.
 
• Instead, it is a significant geological belt in central India that is rich in mineral resources, including coal and other minerals like limestone, bauxite, and manganese.

questions.question: Which of the following isotopes is used as a fuel in nuclear power plants for generating electricity?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Uranium - 235**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Uranium-235 (U-235)** is a fissile isotope, meaning it can sustain a chain reaction of nuclear fission.
 
• U-235 is used as fuel in **nuclear power plants** to generate electricity.
 
• It is one of the few materials that can undergo nuclear fission, making it crucial for nuclear reactors and nuclear weapons.
 
• Uranium-235 is naturally occurring, but only about **0.7% of natural uranium** is U-235, the rest being Uranium-238.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Nuclear Fission**

 
 
• It is the process of splitting a heavy nucleus into two lighter nuclei, accompanied by the release of a large amount of energy.
 
• In a nuclear reactor, when a U-235 nucleus absorbs a neutron, it becomes unstable and splits, releasing energy, more neutrons, and fission products.
 
• The additional neutrons can further induce fission in other U-235 nuclei, creating a self-sustaining chain reaction.
 
 
 
• **Nuclear Power Plants**
 
 
• These facilities use the heat generated from nuclear fission to produce steam, which drives turbines connected to generators, thus producing electricity.
 
• They are considered a low carbon energy source as they do not produce carbon dioxide during operation, unlike fossil fuel-based power plants.
 
 
 
• **Isotopes**
 
 
• Isotopes are variants of a chemical element that have the same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons in their nuclei.
 
• This results in different atomic masses for the isotopes of the same element.
 
 
 
• **Uranium Enrichment**
 
 
• The process of increasing the proportion of U-235 in natural uranium to make it suitable for use in nuclear reactors or weapons.
 
• Enrichment is typically required because natural uranium's U-235 content is too low for most nuclear reactors.
 
• Common methods of enrichment include gas centrifuge and gaseous diffusion.

questions.question: Which National Waterway runs from Haldia to Prayagraj?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**National Waterway 1**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **National Waterway 1** runs from **Haldia to Prayagraj**.
 
• The National Waterway 1 (NW-1), also known as the Ganga-Bhagirathi-Hooghly river system, spans from Prayagraj in Uttar Pradesh to Haldia in West Bengal, traversing through Patna and Bhagalpur in Bihar along the Ganges river.
 
• Stretching over 1,620 km (1,010 mi), NW-1 holds the distinction of being India's longest waterway.
 
• Renowned for its strategic location, NW-1 passes through several states including West Bengal, Jharkhand, Bihar, and Uttar Pradesh, connecting major cities
 
• Designated as a national waterway in October 1986, NW-1 facilitates navigation by mechanical boats up to Patna, playing a pivotal role in inland water transportation in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **National Waterway 2 (NW-2)** is a segment of the Brahmaputra River stretching over 891 kilometers. It extends from the Bangladesh border near Dhubri to Sadiya in Assam. Officially designated as NW-2 on September 1, 1988, this waterway plays a crucial role in inland navigation in the northeastern region of India.
 
• **National Waterway 3 (NW-3) **spans 205 kilometers and serves as an inland navigational route in Kerala, India. Running from Kollam to Kottapuram, NW-3 was declared a National Waterway in 1993, facilitating transportation and trade within the state of Kerala.
 
• **National Waterway 4 (NW-4)** covers a distance of 1,095 kilometers, linking the Indian states of Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, and the union territory of Puducherry. This waterway connects the Krishna and Godavari rivers, serving as a vital transportation route for cargo and passenger movement in the region.

questions.question: According to Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas, Government of India (2021-2022), which state in India is the largest producer of natural gas?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Assam**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Assam:-**

 
 
• According to the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas, Government of India (2021-2022), Assam is the largest producer of natural gas in India. Here are some bullet points to explain the answer:
 
• Assam accounts for about 53% of India's total natural gas production.
 
• The state has several natural gas fields, including the Digboi, Naharkatiya, and Rudrasagar fields.
 
• The production of natural gas in Assam has been increasing steadily over the years. In 2019-20, the state produced over 5,000 million cubic meters of natural gas.
 
• The natural gas produced in Assam is used for various purposes, including power generation, industrial use, and domestic use. 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Andhra Pradesh:-**

 
 
• Andhra Pradesh is not a significant producer of natural gas. 
 
• The state has some natural gas reserves, but they are not yet fully developed. 
 
 
 
• **Maharashtra:**
 
 
• Maharashtra is the second-largest producer of natural gas in India.
 
• The state has several natural gas fields, including the Mumbai High field, which is one of the largest offshore fields in the world.
 
 
 
• **Tamil Nadu:**
 
 
• Tamil Nadu is not a significant producer of natural gas.
 
• The state has some natural gas reserves, but they are not yet fully developed.
